title: Budgets: fifteen a month per person, a draft's Claude budget raised, the Needs-you list as a dropdown, and testers' actions kept under their name
request: The owner asked for a button to add to a session's budget, a fifteen-dollar limit for every signed-in person, every such action saved, the Needs-you panel as a dropdown, and sign-in for trusted friends with everything they do recorded.
spec: dclab_rnd limits (the default, a person's own in budgets.json), the gateway's per-person cap, the twin budget raise and its route, the member budget routes and the Admin controls, the Home dropdown, the person on every twin row, docs/guides/TESTERS.md.
plan: Make the person's monthly limit fifteen and let the owner set one person's own.
Let a draft's Claude budget be raised within the person's room this month, recorded three ways.
Name the person on everything the twin keeps.

decisions.decision: A raise never passes what is left of the person's month or fifteen a draft.
decisions.why: The person's limit is the bound the owner set; a draft cannot spend around it.

decisions.decision: The gateway reads people's own limits from its workspace's folder, not from the request's context.
decisions.why: Inside a twin run's lanes the context has no workspace store, and the owner's limit would have fallen back to the default.

change: dclab_rnd/limits.py, models/gateway.py, agentic/services.py, twin/home.py, draft/api.py, agentic/pages/twin.py, agentic/routers/projects.py, accounts/guard.py, web views home and admin, .env.example, docs; tests in test_twin_home and test_limits.

findings.defect: Concurrent updates to a draft's session file were lost or read half-written.
findings.scenario: A turn's spend and a raise at once lost one of them; two raises at once had one effect.
findings.cause: Each request made its own lock, the raise read outside any lock, and the file was rewritten in place.
findings.fix: One lock per folder for every instance, the raise read and written under it, and the file replaced whole.

findings.defect: A raised draft stopped following the workspace default.
findings.scenario: The owner raised the default above a draft's raised cap and the draft stayed lower.
findings.cause: The draft's own cap replaced the default.
findings.fix: The cap is the higher of the two.

findings.defect: A request with a typo cleared a person's limit.
findings.scenario: Sending monthly instead of monthly_eur returned success and cleared it.
findings.cause: A missing key read as null.
findings.fix: The route refuses a request without the key.

findings.defect: Inside a twin run the owner's limit for a person fell back to the default.
findings.scenario: A person limited to five could spend up to fifteen in a project's twin run.
findings.cause: The limit was read from the request's context, which a lane does not carry.
findings.fix: The gateway carries its workspace's folder, the raise and the run read the person's room from it, and a twin run is capped by that room.

findings.defect: The docs still said twenty-five and the refusal named a setting.
findings.scenario: The settings example and the refusal text pointed at the old default and an environment variable.
findings.cause: They were written before the change.
findings.fix: Fifteen in the example and the refusal points to the owner's Admin control.

findings.scenario: The commit would have lacked its records.
findings.fix: Records are written with the reviewer's findings.

findings.defect: New write routes did not say what they record.
findings.scenario: The session-record test listed the twin message, pick, understanding and settings routes as unrecorded.
findings.cause: The routes were added without their events.
findings.fix: A message to Claude alone is a person's chat event, a pick and the switches are decisions, each route says so.

findings.defect: The Home routes reached into the draft store's folder.
findings.scenario: The storage rule found a path joined from the store's home.
findings.cause: A fallback for tests without services built the workspace path from the store.
findings.fix: The fallback reads the configured workspace folder.

findings.defect: Testers' actions in the twin folder did not say whose they were.
findings.scenario: Trusted friends will test; the owner wants everything they do kept.
findings.cause: The folder kept turns and picks without the person.
findings.fix: Every Claude turn, message, pick and raise names the account it was for, and the session lists its people.

outcome: Budgets work per person and per draft, recorded; testers have a guide and their actions are named.
lessons: A lock that each request creates locks nothing.
Carry the workspace on the object that needs it rather than reading it from a context that may not be there.
risks: The testers must reach the server: a deployment or a tunnel is the owner's decision.
